intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Silver Spring for 2026, and here is what he found: 4 family events, 1 of them free. The magic runs from November 28 (Holly TrolleyFest at the National Capital Trolley Museum) through January 1 (the Festival of Lights in Kensington), with The Mini-Nut by Maryland Youth Ballet (December 5 and 6) along the way. We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.

  • Meet Santa: Holly TrolleyFest rides with Santa and Mrs. Claus (weekends from November 28)

name: Silver Spring
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Silver Spring, MD for 2026: trolley rides with Santa, a free festival of lights and holiday ballet, with dates checked.
lede: Silver Spring families ride a historic trolley with Santa and Mrs. Claus, walk a free festival of lights in Kensington and catch holiday ballet on Georgia Avenue.
celebrates: Silver Spring spreads its Christmas across a few neighborhood traditions rather than one big downtown event. The National Capital Trolley Museum in the Colesville area runs Holly TrolleyFest on weekends from November 28, with Santa and Mrs. Claus riding historic streetcars along a mile-long woodland railway. The Washington DC Temple Visitors' Center in nearby Kensington lights its grounds nightly with a free Festival of Lights from December 2 to January 1, and families need a timed parking pass. Maryland Youth Ballet brings The Mini-Nut to the Montgomery College Cultural Arts Center on Georgia Avenue for younger audiences on December 5 and 6.
lastyear: We did not find a published 2025 recap for Silver Spring's holiday events, so this page leans on each host's 2026 listing. The National Capital Trolley Museum's Holly TrolleyFest page shows photos from its 2025 season, which suggests the weekend rides with Santa are an annual tradition rather than a one-off. The museum also runs a food drive for Olney Help during the festival, and families who bring a nonperishable donation get 10 percent off the museum gift shop on the day of their visit.
facts: The National Capital Trolley Museum runs historic streetcars along a mile-long woodland railway at its Colesville site. Holly TrolleyFest adds a holiday model railroad display built with the Washington, Virginia and Maryland Garden Railway Society, plus children's crafts, a scavenger hunt and hot chocolate. The museum says unused tickets count as a donation, and trolley rides leave about 10 minutes after the ticketed admission time, so plan to arrive a little early.
trains: Silver Spring's holiday train is a trolley. The National Capital Trolley Museum's Holly TrolleyFest runs on Saturdays and Sundays from November 28, with a historic streetcar ride where Santa and Mrs. Claus greet riders and sing carols. A Holiday Woodland Ride at 1:30 pm each festival day goes without them. Admission is $15 per person, children 2 and under are free, and advance tickets are required. The museum is also listed on our train museums guide.

faq: How does Silver Spring celebrate Christmas?

Families ride historic streetcars with Santa at the National Capital Trolley Museum, walk the free Festival of Lights in Kensington and see holiday ballet at Montgomery College. The traditions are spread across the area rather than gathered in one downtown event.
Is there a Santa train near Silver Spring?

Yes. Holly TrolleyFest at the National Capital Trolley Museum runs Saturdays and Sundays from November 28. Santa and Mrs. Claus greet riders on a historic streetcar. Admission is $15 per person and children 2 and under are free.
Is the Kensington Festival of Lights free?
Yes. The Washington DC Temple Visitors' Center lists it as free, and families need a timed parking pass. It runs nightly from December 2 to January 1.
Can toddlers go to Holly TrolleyFest?
Children 2 and under are admitted free. Advance tickets are required for everyone else, and rides depart about 10 minutes after your ticketed admission time.
